title: Rebalance Pages navigation and reading space on narrow viewports
description:
Problem: the live `/pages` review showed both the navigation tree and rendered page fighting for vertical space on narrow viewports. The navigation tree shows only a few rows, the reader pane has its own short scroll area, and code blocks add another horizontal scroller inside the already constrained content area.

Desired outcome: Pages should preserve always-available navigation while giving the selected page enough reading/editing space to feel usable.

Scope:
- In scope: responsive navigation/detail proportions, compact tree header, optional navigation drawer/peek mode, code-block overflow treatment, and focus-reading transitions that preserve discoverability.
- Out of scope: changing page storage or markdown parsing semantics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Narrow-width Pages view shows a useful amount of selected page content without forcing users through multiple small nested scroll areas.
- Navigation remains discoverable and quick to reopen.
- Code blocks do not dominate or awkwardly trap horizontal scrolling in the first viewport.
- Existing Tree/Flat/ToC modes remain reachable and understandable.

Validation:
- Capture `/pages` screenshots for Tree, Flat, ToC, and focus-reading states.
- Run Pages route-smoke/navigation-freeze checks after layout changes.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from 2026-05-25 live visual review: `/pages` keeps navigation visible, but the narrow view leaves both the tree and reader in short nested scroll regions with limited reading room.
